newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse closes 0.25 pct higher.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse closes 0.25 pct higher.

text.p: Morocco's bourse, contining an upward trend, closed on Tuesday 0.25 percent higher, pulled by blue chip firms, including SNI conglomerate, brokers said.
The all-share index closed at 665.62 points, up from 663.99 on Monday, a bourse official said.
"Blue chip share prices continue to rise as a result of increasing demand on the market...Traders do not expect any significant change in the coming days," a stockbroker at Upline Securities said.
But total traded volume was down to 129.3 million dirhams from 144.8 million on Monday.
Electronic trading volume rose to 7.6 million dirhams representing 10,782 shares, of which 9,633 shares were of oil refinery Samir, the stockbroker said.
The volume was 4.1 million dirhams on Monday, or 4,497 shares, including 1,865 Samir shares.
At present, only five firms are traded through the electronic system, including BMCE Bank and steel giant Sonasid.
Samir closed lower at 337 dirhams, down 2.10 dirhams over the previous session.
BMCE, a liquid stock, gained four dirhams to close at 599 dirhams while Sonasid jumped 14 dirhams to 585 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement (SNI), Morocco's second largest private group, was up nine dirhams to close at 786 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie, one of seven active banks on the bourse, rose 13 dirhams to 473 dirhams.
Continuing a medium-term strategy to reinforce shareholders' equity, BMCI recently increased its capital to 742.5 million dirhams ($74.25 million) from 618.75 million dirhams, brokers said.
The Casablanca bourse exchanges on the official market were up to 41.5 million dirhams from 21.3 million dirhams the previous session.
